title: How to Stop Land Grabbing and Illegal Occupation in Bangladesh When You Live Abroad
metaTitle: Land Grabbing in Bangladesh: Legal Remedies for NRBs (Civil & Criminal)
metaDescription: Is someone occupying your land in Bangladesh while you live abroad? Learn the civil and criminal remedies: injunction, recovery of possession, forgery cases and how to prevent grabbing.
keywords: illegal occupation of land Bangladesh remedy
heroIntro: Land grabbing is the number one fear of Non-Resident Bangladeshis. A relative builds a house on your plot, a neighbour extends a boundary wall, or a stranger produces a forged deed. The longer you wait, the harder recovery becomes. This guide is written by Advocate Md. Shah Alam, Supreme Court of Bangladesh, for Bangladeshis living in the UK, USA, UAE, Canada and elsewhere. For case-specific help call or WhatsApp the chamber on 01712655546.

quickAnswer.heading: Land Grabbing: Quick Answers
points: Act within days: collect evidence, send a legal notice and file for an injunction before the occupier builds or sells.
Civil remedies: suit for declaration of title, recovery of possession and permanent injunction (Specific Relief Act 1877).
If you were dispossessed without lawful process, a suit under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act within six months does not require proof of title.
Criminal remedies: criminal trespass, cheating and forgery under the Penal Code 1860; file a case or an FIR.
Prevention is cheaper than cure: mutation, land tax receipts, boundary pillars, a caretaker and regular site visits.

toc: Common Ways NRB Land Is Grabbed

sections.h2: Common Ways NRB Land Is Grabbed
sections.content:
• A relative or caretaker builds on the land and later claims ownership.
  • Fake deeds or a forged Power of Attorney are used to sell your land.
  • Boundary encroachment by neighbours, slowly over years.
  • Local "syndicates" occupy vacant plots and demand money.
  • Wrong mutation (Namjari) entered in another person's name.

This article is general legal information, not legal advice. Fees, forms and procedures change; confirm current requirements with the relevant office or a qualified advocate before acting.

Evidence wins land cases. Ask a trusted person to visit and:

  • Take dated photos and video showing the occupier, structures and boundary.
  • Collect statements of neighbours and local members/chairman.
  • Get certified copies of your deed, Khatian and mutation record (see how to check land records online).
  • Obtain the occupier's claimed documents, if any, and ask your advocate to check them.
  • Make a General Diary (GD) at the nearest police station recording the threat or occupation.

A short legal notice from an advocate often resolves disputes with relatives or neighbours. It creates a record, shows you are serious and prevents the occupier from claiming you consented. Give a clear deadline (usually 7 to 15 days) to vacate or show documents. Do not skip this step if the occupier is a family member; it also helps judges later.

The Civil Court is the main forum for ownership and possession:

  • Suit for declaration of title and recovery of possession: you must prove title. The usual limit is 12 years from dispossession, so do not delay.
  • Suit under Section 9, Specific Relief Act 1877: if you were dispossessed without your consent and not through due process of law, you can file within six months and the court will restore possession without deciding title.
  • Temporary and permanent injunction (Section 54, Specific Relief Act): stops the occupier from building, selling or transferring the land while the case continues.
  • Cancellation of a forged deed or wrong mutation: to clear your record.

Ask for an ad-interim injunction at the very beginning; it is the most valuable relief for NRBs.

If force, forgery or cheating is involved, criminal law can apply in parallel:

  • Criminal trespass (Penal Code 1860, Sections 441-447).
  • Cheating and dishonest inducement (Section 420) for fraudulent sale.
  • Forgery and using forged documents (Sections 463-471).
  • Criminal intimidation (Section 506).

Police or the Magistrate may also act under Section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure where there is a dispute likely to cause a breach of the peace. You can file a petition of complaint with the Magistrate if the police refuse. For emergencies you can also call the national helpline 999.

Meanwhile, apply to the Assistant Commissioner (Land) to correct a wrong mutation, and keep paying land development tax. A petition to the Deputy Commissioner and Superintendent of Police documenting the threat can also help. These are supporting steps and do not replace the court case. Your lawyer will advise which to use. See also our Power of Attorney guide so your representative can act for you.

1. Complete mutation and pay tax every year.
  2. Build a boundary wall and place a signboard with your name and contact.
  3. Appoint a paid caretaker and avoid giving long-term free occupation to relatives.
  4. Give only limited, special Powers of Attorney and review them each year.
  5. Keep digital copies of all documents with your advocate.
  6. Visit once a year, or ask your advocate for a regular report.
  7. Register any tenancy or licence in writing with an end date.

This article is general legal information, not legal advice. Fees, forms and procedures change; confirm current requirements with the relevant office or a qualified advocate before acting.

faqs.question: Can I file a land grabbing case from abroad?
faqs.answer: Yes. Your advocate can file the suit with a Power of Attorney, and some hearings can proceed without your presence. You may need to give evidence later, sometimes by video.

faqs.question: How long do I have to recover land in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: A suit for possession based on title generally must be filed within 12 years of dispossession, and a Section 9 suit within six months. Do not wait.

faqs.question: Can a relative take my land by living on it for many years?
faqs.answer: Long adverse possession can create rights after the limitation period, so you should act when you first learn about the occupation.

faqs.question: What is an injunction?
faqs.answer: A court order that stops a person from selling, building on or transferring land until the case is decided.

faqs.question: Should I file a criminal case or a civil case?
faqs.answer: If there is forgery, fraud or force, you may do both. Civil cases decide title and possession; criminal cases punish wrongdoing.
